# Gross domestic product

## Gross domestic product

Gross domestic product is the total market value of all final goods and services produced within a country in a given period. Only final goods are counted, because counting intermediate goods as well would count the same value twice. Real GDP adjusts for changes in prices, while nominal GDP does not. Economists use real GDP to compare output across different years.

## Limits

GDP does not include unpaid work such as housework or volunteering. GDP per person divides total GDP by the population and is often used as a rough measure of average living standards. A high GDP per person does not show how income is distributed among residents. Illegal and unreported activity is largely missing from official GDP figures. Statistics agencies in most countries publish a new GDP estimate every 3 months.
